newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U sees restructuring ready early next century.
newsitem.headline: P&U sees restructuring ready early next century.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Wednesday that it will finalise restructuring at the beginning of the next century.
"We have said that we will decrease our plants by 40 percent to just over 30," company spokesman Soren Densjo told Reuters, adding the number of employees would fall.

"This means that we will start up new plants while selling and divesting others," he said. "It's a long process that will last three to six years and we won't be done until sometime into the next century."
The group will, for example, set up a plant for contact lenses in India and other plants in China, while several closures will in fact mean selling production to other pharmaceutical companies.

"All our plants are ultramodern and we will surely be able to find solutions where we sell plants to other drugs groups, as when we sold the Malmo (Sweden) plant to Ferring and the Arsta (Sweden) plant to Recip," he said.
"In none of these cases were employees laid off."
Pharmacia & Upjohn will also focus development of new drugs to plants where manufacturing of similar products exists.
"You cannot forget that during this time (of restructuring) we will launch new products," Densjo said. "It is likely that we will try to increase utilisation of existing plants."
The cutback of plants is one measure in a five point programme aiming to increase profitability.

The programme also contains investments to increase the rate of product launches as well as improved strategy and planning through one and three year plans. In 1997, the group will invest $150 million, Densjo said.
The company will also get a new organisation with three units: Prescription Pharmaceuticals, Associated Businesses and Investment Holdings.
It will also focus and concentrate operations as well as improve asset management, change currency hedgings and increase capital turnover.
The programme also follows profitability problems. The group has issued a couple of profit warnings which have sent its shares tumbling on the New York and Stockholm stock exchanges.

It latest warning came less than a week before it was due to release first quarter earnings. In the first three months of the year, its sales dropped 6.1 percent to $1.64 billion while earnings per share fell to $0.37 from $0.44.
